object_description: staggered clinic ensemble of parallel and transverse volumes
design_condition: The building follows the existing edge and slope, creating a three-sided open-space ensemble with a small park on the mountain side, while excavations and an undefined opening weaken its relationship to the neighbourhood and park.

positive.statement: The center-and-periphery concept offers a promising basis for an ensemble with the existing buildings.

position.rationale: The top view directly shows a central composition surrounded by offset peripheral volumes.

positive.statement: Staggered heights and facade setbacks adapt the building to the district and achieve a compatible scale.

position.rationale: Stepped outer edges and differing elevation bands visibly establish setbacks and height variation.

positive.statement: The small mountain-side park can serve as open space for both the district and the clinic.

position.rationale: The park is not separately sampled; the open northern side beyond the ensemble is the plausible landscape anchor.

positive.statement: The entrance situation on Hofstrasse is clear and uncluttered.

position.rationale: The entrance is unnamed geometrically; a lower perimeter access point provides a constrained arrival estimate.

positive.statement: The entrance hall creates a cheerful atmosphere and an attractive interplay between indoor and outdoor spaces.

position.rationale: Interior hall is not visible, so the lower access-facing volume is used as an approximate anchor.

positive.statement: The clinic-room arrangement enables the desired separation between staff and patients.

position.rationale: Room organization is interior and indistinguishable; the substantial eastern block provides a useful zone estimate.

positive.statement: The polyclinic can be converted to a new use with only a few structural interventions.

position.rationale: The converted component cannot be identified; the offset western volume is a constrained approximation.

positive.statement: The connection to the new building is a precise and coherent intervention inherent in the existing typology and concept.

position.rationale: A central joining zone is visibly suggested where the principal bars and transverse volume meet.

positive.statement: The urban-planning concept is robust with regard to future preservation, replacement, or release of the sisters' house.

position.rationale: The broad urban-planning judgment is anchored to the eastern perimeter of the visible ensemble.

positive.statement: The result is valuable for the historical inventory and its perception.

position.rationale: This broad identity judgment is placed on a prominent western mass visible across the ensemble.

positive.statement: The independent facade forms an ensemble with the character buildings while creating a familiar expression.

position.rationale: The stepped eastern facade visibly reads as an independent but coordinated edge.

positive.statement: The hybrid wood-concrete construction conceptually takes sustainability requirements into account.

position.rationale: Material construction is not represented by the sampled geometry and applies to the whole building.

positive.statement: Resource-saving and lean materialization compensate to a large extent for the effort required under the terrain.

position.rationale: Resource efficiency and material economy are whole-building judgments without a spatially specific marker.

negative.statement: The green space along Pestalozzistrasse has little quality and resembles distance green.

position.rationale: The street edge is unlabeled; the southern open margin provides a constrained site anchor.

negative.statement: The opening toward the neighbourhood lacks a clear spatial definition.

position.rationale: The undefined opening is approximated at the broad northeastern edge where the ensemble opens outward.

negative.statement: The proposed excavation along the north-east facade can hardly be approved under building regulations in its current form.

position.rationale: The northeast facade is directionally and geometrically anchored on the upper-right perimeter.

negative.statement: The three atriums obscure the relationship between the new building and the park.

position.rationale: Repeated interruptions and open voids are visible within the central ensemble, though individual atriums are not fully separable.

negative.statement: The paths are functional, but a self-confident park character is missing.

position.rationale: External routes are not sampled distinctly; the southern perimeter is used for the constrained landscape-circulation judgment.

negative.statement: The main entrance appears too large and too stony.

position.rationale: The oversized entrance is not identifiable, so the lower access-facing edge provides an approximate anchor.

negative.statement: The adjacent seating area does not appear self-evident, and preserving the existing trees will hardly be possible.

position.target: adjacent seating area and existing trees
position.rationale: Landscape furnishings and trees are absent; the southern edge beside the entrance is the constrained site location.

negative.statement: The sudden transitions from the large entrance hall to corridors and stairwells were critically assessed.

position.rationale: The hall-to-corridor sequence is interior; the lower entry block provides a constrained approximation.

negative.statement: Crossing access routes and internal clinic waiting rooms are spatially and operationally problematic.

position.target: clinic waiting rooms and access routes
position.rationale: Internal waiting and circulation spaces are not distinguishable, so the central connector is used as an estimate.

negative.statement: The underground teaching area without daylight did not convince the jury.

position.rationale: The below-grade area is not visible directly; the lowest sampled building level provides the constrained anchor.

negative.statement: There is no direct connection between teaching and research without passing through the clinics.

position.rationale: The internal connection cannot be seen; the transverse central connector is the most plausible spatial proxy.

negative.statement: The wooden roller shutters do not optimally meet the requirements for shading and daylight control.

position.rationale: Shutters are not resolved; the exposed eastern facade provides the directional facade anchor.

negative.statement: The contribution is one of the more complex proposals in terms of economic efficiency.

position.rationale: Economic complexity is a whole-project judgment without a useful geometric location.

negative.statement: The project requires relatively large floor area and underbuilds a significant part of the plot.

position.target: large floor area and plot underbuilding
position.rationale: The broad footprint is directly visible in plan and occupies most of the sampled site envelope.

negative.statement: The insulation, airtightness, facade construction, and summer thermal protection require further development to achieve the required standard.

position.rationale: Envelope performance is anchored to the exposed eastern facade, where the relevant systems would occur.

negative.statement: Spatially dividing excavations and weak relationships between the garden and new building contradict the idea of strengthening the hospital garden as a center.

position.rationale: The northeastern edge is the stated excavation and garden-facing zone, approximated from the ensemble perimeter.
